{{short description|British biologist}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
'''Patricia Simpson''' is a British developmental biologist. Simpson was a professor of Comparative Biology at the University of Cambridge from 2003 to 2010, and was the university's Director of Research for the academic year 2010/2011.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Honorary Fellows – Newnham College|url=https://www.newn.cam.ac.uk/about/people/honorary-fellows/|access-date=2020-10-24|website=www.newn.cam.ac.uk}}</ref> She is currently an emeritus Professor of the Department of Zoology of the [[University of Cambridge]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Professor Pat Simpson FRS|url=https://www.zoo.cam.ac.uk/directory/emeritus-professor-pat-simpson|website=Department of Zoology|publisher=University of Cambridge|accessdate=30 June 2016}}</ref> having previously been Professor of Comparative Embryology,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.zoo.cam.ac.uk/zoostaff/simpson.htm |title=Zoology: Simpson |accessdate=2010-05-04 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20100302205736/http://www.zoo.cam.ac.uk/zoostaff/simpson.htm |archivedate=2010-03-02 }}</ref> and a Fellow of [[Newnham College]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.newn.cam.ac.uk/seniormembers/pas49.shtml |title=Archived copy |accessdate=2010-05-04 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20100706074917/http://www.newn.cam.ac.uk/seniormembers/pas49.shtml |archivedate=2010-07-06 }}</ref> She was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] in 2000.<ref>{{cite web|title=Patricia Simpson|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/patricia-simpson-12281/|website=Fellows Directory|publisher=Royal Society|accessdate=30 June 2016}}</ref>

Patricia Simpson graduated with her PhD in 1976<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=2008-05-06|title=Patricia Simpson|url=http://wils-database.embo.org/members_meet.php?action=member&aus=1&member_id=171|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2020-10-27|website=WiLS Database - Women in Life Sciences}}</ref> from Universite de Paris VI, [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://wils.database.embo.org/members_meet.php?action=member&aus=1&member_id=171 |title=WiLS Database - Expert Women in Life Sciences |accessdate=2010-05-04 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110726024831/http://wils.database.embo.org/members_meet.php?action=member&aus=1&member_id=171 |archivedate=2011-07-26 }}</ref>
Her research interests include organismal biology, evolution, and ecology, and she is distinguished for her work on insect development and evolution. Specifically, her research explores the pattern formation of sensory bristles in fruit flies.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Patricia Simpson {{!}} Royal Society|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/patricia-simpson-12281/|access-date=2020-10-24|website=royalsociety.org|language=en-gb}}</ref> Her first major discovery was that pattern formation and growth of fly bristles are regulated by the same mechanism. By a study of genetic mosaics she demonstrated that cells develop into particular structures by means of local interactions with their neighbours.

She has made major contributions to the understanding of the process of [[lateral inhibition]], whereby initially equivalent cells interact between themselves and subsequently adopt different fates. 
This process involves a conserved [[cellular receptor]] and is equally important in mammals; the work can be related to studies on human development and disease.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://f1000biology.com/about/biography/1159512888132299 |title=Patricia Simpson: Former F1000Prime Faculty Member in Developmental Molecular Mechanisms - F1000Prime |website=F1000biology.com |date= |accessdate=2016-06-30}}</ref>

==Awards==
* 1993: Silver medal of the Centre National de la Recherche Scientifque, France
* 1993: She was elected as the member of the [[European Molecular Biology Organization|EMBO]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=EMBO Members Directory |url=https://people.embo.org/profile/patricia-simpson}}</ref>
* 2000: [[Fellow of the Royal Society]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Emeritus Professor Patricia Simpson FRS {{!}} Royal Society Fellow |url=https://royalsociety.org/people/patricia-simpson-12281/ |access-date=2026-05-18 |website=royalsociety.org |language=en}}</ref>
*2008: Waddington Medal of the [[British Society for Developmental Biology|British Society of Developmental Biology]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Waddington Medal |url=https://bsdb.org/awards/the-waddington-medal/ |access-date=2026-05-18 |website=BSDB - British Society for Developmental Biology |language=en-US}}</ref>
*2012: Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=AAAS Members Elected as Fellows |url=https://www.aaas.org/news/aaas-members-elected-fellows-0}}</ref>
*2016:  Honorary Fellowship from [[Newnham College, Cambridge|Newnham College]], Cambridge<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-02-13 |title=Pat Simpson {{!}} Newnham College |url=https://newn.cam.ac.uk/person/pat-simpson |access-date=2026-05-18 |website=newn.cam.ac.uk |language=en}}</ref>
